subject: Dedicated reservation: workload fitment & GPU mix Q&A
messages:
From: Miriam Stone <miriam.stone@apollocorp.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Devon Lee <devon.lee@apollocorp.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFI: Dedicated reservation sizing questionnaire

Hi Irene,

Thanks for agreeing to take a look — we've put together a short workload profile (attached) and a few clarifying questions to help us size a dedicated pool with your platform. High level background: ApolloCorp is building an in-product assistant for our analytics product. Latency sensitivity on the primary route is p95 < 500ms. Average prompt/response is ~220 tokens, we have a small embedding pipeline for search (~2k QPS of small vectors). We expect steady-state traffic of ~110 requests/sec for generation with peak bursts up to ~350 requests/sec for 20-30 minute windows after feature launches.

Specifics we'd like you to confirm in your response:
- Recommended GPU families for mixed workload (chat generation + embeddings) and approximate count for a 12-month reservation.
- Expected sustained throughput (req/s) per GPU for a 70B-class generation model at ~220 tokens average (assume fp16 and no quantization initially).
- Safe burst capacity you can plan for without impacting p95 SLA and recommended guardrails.
- Any cache/prefix strategies we should enable to reduce token costs for short repeated prompts.
- Fallback/auto-scale plans (model variants, quantized fallback, region overflow).

I've attached the workload CSV — it includes time-of-day distribution and token length percentiles. Happy to hop on a quick call if it's easier.

Thanks,
Miriam
Miriam Stone
Head of ML Infrastructure
ApolloCorp

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-05-04T13:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Dedicated reservation sizing questionnaire

Hi Miriam — thanks for the profile, that was helpful. I've summarized answers inline and attached a short sizing workbook (redwood-dedicated-gpu-sizing.xlsx) with two reservation options (conservative and aggressive). High level recommendations below; we'll expand numbers in the workbook.

Summary answers:
- GPU families: For your mix we recommend a blended pool: H100-80GB (primary for high-throughput 70B chat with low p95) + A100-80GB (cost-effective for embeddings and parallel inference). We also include a small set of L4s for small, low-cost inference (light-weight routing).
- Throughput guidance (sustained, single-GPU):
  * H100-80GB (fp16, 70B-class): ~12-16 requests/sec sustained at 220-token avg with p95 latency target <= 500ms when using continuous batching and RBC packing.
  * A100-80GB (fp16, 70B-class): ~8-12 requests/sec sustained for the same workload; better density for batched embeddings.
  * L4 (int8/quantized small models): used for low-cost routing and microservices (chat pre-processing, safety checks).
- Reservation recommendation (12-month) — conservative vs. aggressive:
  * Conservative: 8 x H100 + 12 x A100 (covers ~120 req/s baseline with 30% headroom, burst handled by reserved burst pool + autoscale)
  * Aggressive: 12 x H100 + 20 x A100 (covers ~220 req/s sustained, simplifies tail-latency during peak).
- Burst handling: Plan a reserved burst lane (elastic pool) equal to ~50-75% of sustained capacity using pre-warmed instances and fast-failover to quantized model variants. For your 350 req/s short bursts, the conservative plan will combine reserved burst + brief cloud burst (pay-as-you-go) to avoid degraded p95.
- Caching strategies: Enable prefix + KV caching for repeated prompts (we estimate 15-25% token reduction for your traffic shape). Use per-route caching policies for the analytics-assistant route and TTLs aligned to your dataset update cadence.
- Fallbacks and quantization: We support automatic model-fallback routing to a 4-bit quantized variant (verified against your eval set) and region overflow. That variant typically reduces cost by ~40% at ~2-4% quality delta in our eval suite.

Attached: redwood-dedicated-gpu-sizing.xlsx (workbook tabs: assumptions, conservative-plan, aggressive-plan, cost-estimate) and redwood-sla-and-fallbacks.pdf (SLA notes, failover behavior). I'll loop Marcus for GPU-packing specifics and Karthik for pricing/contract layout.

Next step: If this looks reasonable, propose a 60-minute sizing workshop where we sketch a mutual action plan and walk the workbook. Availability: May 6-7 (US mornings) works for us.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Thanks Irene — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A few follow-ups after scanning the workbook:

1) Can you confirm the benchmarking assumptions for the H100 numbers (sequence length, batch strategy)? We want to ensure the 12-16 rps/GPU assumes dynamic batching with avg batch size ~6 and sequence length = 220 output tokens + 60 prompt tokens.
2) Do you have guidance on how quickly the reserved burst lane can spin up for a sudden national campaign spike? We need a <5min warm-up for pre-warmed reserved bursts ideally.
3) Pricing: ballpark monthly committed cost for the conservative recommendation (8x H100 + 12x A100) including typical 12-month discount tier. Even a +/- 15% estimate is helpful for our procurement.

Also — on fallbacks: what's your process for validating the 4-bit variant against our prompt set? Are there automated eval hooks we can run?

If possible let's take the workshop on May 6 at 10:00 AM PT. Devon and I will both join.

—Miriam

On Thu, May 6, 2027 at 08:41 AM, Miriam Stone <miriam.stone@apollocorp.com> wrote:
> 1) Can you confirm the benchmarking assumptions for the H100 numbers (sequence length, batch strategy)?

Yes — benchmark assumptions used to produce the worksheet: sequence length = 280 tokens (avg prompt 60 + avg response 220), dynamic batching with target batch size 5–8 (depends on request arrival), mixed-size packing enabled, and kv/prefix cache hit rate set to 18% for typical dashboard queries. We include an appendix in the workbook detailing the baseline perf runs and scripts.

> 2) Do you have guidance on how quickly the reserved burst lane can spin up for a sudden national campaign spike?

Reserved burst lanes are pre-warmed; typical spin-up time to accept traffic is under 2 minutes for reserved pool instances (they remain warm). If you need warm start for additional cloud burst capacity, plan for a ~3–6 minute warm-up depending on region and instance availability. We'll work with our capacity ops to pre-stage additional warm hosts for campaign windows.

> 3) Pricing: ballpark monthly committed cost for the conservative recommendation (8x H100 + 12x A100) including typical 12-month discount tier.

High-level ballpark (sensitive; indicative only): committed monthly platform + infra blended rate ~ $180k–$230k / month for the conservative config after standard committed discounts. Exact pricing depends on purchase terms (upfront vs. monthly), volume credits, and data egress assumptions — Karthik will follow up with a formal quote during the workshop.

> Fallback validation for 4-bit variant

We provide an automated regression harness: you can supply a representative prompt set (we can reuse the CSV you already provided). The harness runs side-by-side comparisons (ROUGE/BLEU + custom evals) and surface per-prompt quality deltas; typical turnaround to get a validation report is 48–72 hours once we have the prompt set and model variant chosen.

Action items / next steps:
- Confirm workshop: May 6, 10:00 AM PT — Marcus will present GPU-packing scenarios; Karthik will bring a draft term sheet.
- We will run an initial quantized-variant validation using a 500-prompt sample you provide (please share by EOD May 6).
- Redwood to update workbook with a three-tiered burst playbook and projected monthly cost ranges for conservative/aggressive plans.

Looking forward — talk on Friday.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
